notes.index 6 / 8 (fee_recipient, buyback_fee_: NOT uniquely derivable — they are a CHOICE from a set held in the Global account. Measured: across 37 sell_v2 instructions, 13 distinct fee recipients (Global.fee_recipient + fee_recipients[7] + reserved_fee_recipient + reserved_fee_recipients[7]) and all 8 buyback_fee_recipients appear. In all 8 slots that carried two or more sell_v2 instructions, the two used DIFFERENT fee recipients AND different buyback recipients — so this is a free client choice, not a slot- or time-derived rotation the encoder must reproduce. Global.fee_recipient (62qc2CNXwrYqQScmEdiZFFAnJR262PxWEuNQtxfafNgV) was used directly by 8 of 13 top-level samples. buyback_fee_recipients[k] for any k in 0..7 was observed landing.
notes.index 14 (associated_base_user): The IDL declares NO pda constraint on this account, and the chain agrees: 62WGYHpFb86fN6sC1LARyrRWs7r476zze11pAcAJeEt9psP6yoShsBTbpgWJg3HAaGJFBBNFWHFro7oDUu549LJK passed CZJPVdMMwcZaoDJEcM8wz9SNEVLbMUqQFYYKdEQGrJ57, a plain (non-ATA) Token-2022 account owned by the signer for the base mint, which it closed in the same transaction. Every other sample passed the canonical ATA. This is a caller degree of freedom, not an encoder hazard: the encoder passes its own ATA and 13 of 14 samples prove the program accepts that.
notes.index 18 (sharing_config) — ON-CHAIN PRO: Two of the derived addresses hold live accounts owned by pfeeUxB6jkeY1Hxd7CsFCAjcbHA9rWtchMGdZ6VojVZ, 1024 bytes, whose first 8 bytes are d84a0900388c5d4b — the exact SharingConfig account discriminator in the IDL (4gBUoByTtjrQqK4QjQqB2biq5tgGdXo4pNpaT9WKxuWp and 7nn6UGVBKPqLLjmV1A9kbYee7o2Tbi41VTwADwgV2RtS). The other derived addresses are uninitialized, which is exactly what the IDL doc comment predicts. This is identification by discriminator and owner, not by name resemblance.
notes.index 18 (sharing_config): The prior measurement called this UNIDENTIFIED_B. It is resolved: findProgramAddress(["sharing-config", base_mint], pfeeUxB6jkeY1Hxd7CsFCAjcbHA9rWtchMGdZ6VojVZ) — the FEE program, not the pump program. It matched all 14 samples exactly. On the fee-sharing coin DRA4qXNRw5XBd5aVBjFdKJWMc1yiBpqrp8gTWYsmpump this PDA is ALSO the value stored in BondingCurve.creator, which is why creator_vault routes creator fees into the sharing config. The account may be uninitialized (the IDL docs say handlers check data_is_empty) — it is passed read-only either way.
notes.the 27th account: Signature 4qjN1NqzU6BhMFUtVbGiJWjxZ16FRieUFWwR3G4HWduXcFjqPaNTRKZtpwuundMLPXhRoGpNWf4kZGrH1T95aRHe, a CPI from router term9YPb9mzAsABaqN71A4xdbxHmpBNZavpBiQKZzN3, appends 9NG51MGpmqYmvpnQE63NzY4TsZW4MijP8VuYBhXMzcT4 at index 26. Indices 0-25 are the standard IDL order. That account does not exist on chain (null account info, 0 lamports before and after), is read-only, and is referenced nowhere else in the transaction except the router instruction that passed it through. I could NOT identify what it is; it is not any PDA I tried under the pump, fee, or router programs. It is an extra remaining-account injected by a third party and is not required: 36 of 37 observed sell_v2 instructions, and 13 of 13 top-level ones, carry exactly 26.
notes.account meta flags: Verified separately: in all 16 top-level samples, every one of the 26 positions carries exactly the writable and signer flag the IDL declares. No position varied.
notes.inner vs top-level: 16 of 17 verified samples are TOP-LEVEL instructions with real account metas. The 14th (3isikUZT5kuk...) is a CPI and is included deliberately: it is the only non-SOL-quoted curve found, and it is the sample that validates the quote_mint ruler.
